whats_working: Consistent card system: every SectionCard shares radii.lg, 1px border, card shadow, and Space Grotesk headings, so the long scroll reads as one calm green/cream system across light and dark (iphone/light 13, ipad/dark 10).

Persistent footer with Back + Submit stays docked and respects insets.bottom (paddingBottom insets.bottom + 12, line 772); the primary Submit CTA sits in the thumb zone on phone and mirrors the in-card Quick-actions submit so intent is discoverable in two places.

Disabled/blocked submit state is honestly communicated: the incomplete-warning line and 'Still incomplete' chip both appear, and submitDisabled dims the CTA to 0.6 opacity (line 800) — good feedback for a locked action.
Dark mode is fully implemented via designSystem.colors, not a light UI dimmed: surfaces, borders, warning text all switch to the dark palette correctly (iphone/dark 13, android-tablet/dark 10).

findings.title: "Not answered" is rendered as a solid primary-green filled pill — the app's highest-emphasis affirmative color used for a missing value
findings.affected: Youth weighting rows + section-header pills; all themes/platforms
findings.evidence: app/audit/[placeId]/review.tsx line 618 sets the weighting badge backgroundColor to theme.accent, and getReviewThemeByStep (line 1247-1253) returns accent = designSystem.colors.primary. In ipad/light 10 and android-tablet/light 11 the 'Not answered' text sits in a dark-green pill identical to the primary 'Submit audit' CTA; in dark mode (iphone/dark 13, android-tablet/dark 11) it becomes a filled mint pill — the same fill as the enabled Submit button. A missing/negative value reads as a confirmed positive badge.
findings.why: The strongest, most affirmative brand color in the app is applied to the ONE state that means 'you have not done this'. Auditors scanning for gaps see solid green pills that look like completion checkmarks, inverting the signal they most need before a locked, irreversible submission.
findings.fix: For empty/negative values, swap theme.accent for a neutral treatment: render 'Not answered' pills with backgroundColor surfaceMuted, borderColor border, and mutedForeground text (or the warning tone via warningSoft + warningText per DESIGN.md soft-background rule). Reserve the primary fill for answered/affirmative values only.

findings.title: Section answer rows print 'Not answered' in primary-green accent text on primarySoft, coloring an empty value with the brand affirmative
findings.affected: Per-question AnswerPill inside each review section
findings.evidence: review.tsx lines 705-710 pass accent={theme.accent} (=primary) and soft={theme.soft} to AnswerPill regardless of whether row.response is 'Not answered'. AnswerPill (line 1071) renders the value in that accent color. In android-phone/light 14 and android-tablet 11 the Access rows show 'Not answered' in the same green pill styling as a real 'Yes?' answer.
findings.why: An unanswered required field and a genuine answer are visually indistinguishable at a glance — both are green accent pills — which defeats the purpose of a pre-submit review screen where the auditor must find and fix gaps.
findings.fix: In the section row map (line 687-720), detect row.response === 'Not answered' and pass a muted/warning tone to AnswerPill (mutedForeground text on surfaceMuted, or warningText on warningSoft) so unfilled answers are visually distinct from answered ones.

findings.title: Tablet review stretches to contentMaxWidth (1040-1200) instead of readableMaxWidth ~760, leaving answer pills floating in dead space and question lines over-long
findings.evidence: review.tsx line 496 calls getResponsiveContentContainerStyle(layout, {...}) with no maxWidth override, so it defaults to layout.contentMaxWidth (responsive-layout-tokens.ts: NARROW 1040 -> WIDE 1200). This is a content-light read-and-confirm detail screen, which the design system caps at readableMaxWidth 760. In ipad/light 11 and android-tablet 11 each answer field spans the full ~1150px with a single short value ('Yes?', 'Not answered') pinned left, and the Access safety question runs the full width as one long line.
findings.why: Long measure and vast empty answer fields make the tablet read like a stretched phone rather than an adapted large-canvas layout; it is harder to scan and looks unfinished versus the spec's centered readable column for detail screens.
findings.fix: Pass maxWidth: layout.formMaxWidth (600) or a readableMaxWidth (~760) to getResponsiveContentContainerStyle on tablet so the review column centers, matching Execute/Reports/Settings. Footer already tracks layout.screenPaddingHorizontal; align it via getContentTrackInnerWidth if the column narrows.

findings.title: 'Still incomplete' / 'Ready to submit' status chip is styled identically to neutral metadata chips
findings.evidence: review.tsx lines 519-521 render the readiness state through the generic Chip component (line 1079-1094: border + surfaceMuted + foreground text) — the exact same style as the 'AUD002', place-name, and '8 saved answers' chips. In iphone/light 13 and ipad/light 10 'Still incomplete' has no color, icon, or weight distinguishing it from static metadata.
findings.why: The single most decision-relevant piece of status on this screen (can I submit?) carries no more emphasis than an ID label, so it is easy to overlook; and if it did convey state only via a future color it would still need a non-color signifier.
findings.fix: Give the readiness chip a tone: warning (warningSoft bg + warningText) when incompleteStep !== null and success (successSoft + successText) when ready, plus a TriangleAlert / CheckCircle2 icon. Reuse the shared Badge primitive (components/ui/Badge with a DesignTone) instead of the bespoke Chip so tone is first-class.

findings.title: Screen hand-rolls SectionCard, Chip, ActionButton, AnswerPill inline instead of shared components/ui primitives
findings.evidence: Pack header 'design_system_components_used: (none)'. review.tsx defines local SectionCard (line 983), Chip (1079), ActionButton (1127), AnswerPill (1042), StepJumpButton (1096) and raw tamagui Button with inline style objects (lines 666-684, 776-820) rather than components/ui Card/SectionCard, Badge, AppButton, ListRow. These shared primitives exist per core.md.
findings.why: Re-implementing primitives inline is exactly how the color/tone regressions above (Not-answered fill, undifferentiated status chip) slipped in — bespoke styling drifts from the system and won't inherit future fixes; it also risks tap-target and radius drift from the shared AppButton/Badge contracts.
findings.fix: Replace inline Buttons with AppButton (primary|secondary|ghost), status chip with Badge, section shells with SectionCard(raised), and the summary rows with ListRow. This centralizes radii.button, 44pt min height, and tone handling.

findings.title: Empty placeholders ('No section comments added.') render at the same weight/color as real answers
findings.evidence: SummaryRow (review.tsx line 1035) renders every value in foreground + bodyMedium. Fallback strings like 'No weighting comments added.' (line 641) and 'No section comments added.' (line 724) get identical styling to substantive data (iphone/dark 14, ipad 11).
findings.why: Placeholders read as content, adding visual noise on an already long scroll and making it fractionally harder to distinguish 'nothing here' from a real short answer.
findings.fix: When the value is a known empty fallback, style it with mutedForeground and italic (or lighter weight) in SummaryRow, so absent data recedes.
